messages:
sam: quick flag 1: onboarding run for 'aurora-mini-ptq' showing weird toolcall ordering under streaming+kvcache. failure rate ~3.9% in the canary.

li: can you show an example of the broken payload?

sam: pasted from logs: 
```
{"req_id":"42","actions":[{"meta":"tmp"},{"name":"translate","args":{"text":"hi"}}],"text":"..."}
```

sam: our contract expects actions[0] to be the tool invocation; postproc rejects when the first element is a filler.

priya: did this start after the PTQ pass? any difference vs fp16 baseline?

sam: baseline fp16 canary had 0.2% of this. ptq on same model jumps to 3.9% when streaming is enabled. Non-stream single shot ~0.4%.

henry: seems correlated with streaming + batching. Could be tokenization/frame boundary slip or KV-cache flushing emitting an interim object.

li: options: 1) make parser tolerant (search for first action.name matching known tool set) 2) add explicit sentinel token or boundary token in generation 3) runtime: mark per-request boundaries in batching so responses don't interleave.

priya: quick mitigation: parser tolerant approach is low-risk. But long term we should avoid relying on heuristics. I like the sentinel idea: have the prompt append a fixed JSON field like "__action_start":true before the tool object. Parser can assert existence.

henry: sentinel works but might be fragile with quantized tokenization (sentinel might split). Maybe emit a short numeric index field like "i":0 which is robust. Runtime can enforce index monotonicity across stream chunks.

sam: implemented a tolerant-match patch that scans the actions array for known tool names and picks the highest-confidence match. Local eval: ptq streaming batch=16 failures drop from 3.9% -> 0.6%.

li: good. but we need evidence before committing. can you run adversarial harness: inject dummy placeholder tokens into prompts and measure parsing rate? record first 5k failures.
sam: started job via ops-bot: run action-ordering-adversarial(aurora-mini-ptq) samples=50k strat=streaming,batch=[1,8,16]. job id 90211.

ops-bot: job 90211 queued. estimated 75m. results to #eng-ml when complete.

priya: also add a small change to the onboarding checklist: require running "ordering-robustness" test for any model that will be used with funcalls.

henry: for runtime fixes, filing an infra ticket: ensure batching respects per-request segment ids so that when we stitch streaming frames we preserve intra-request order. This may require tagging frames with request-id+seq and enforcing merge order rather than naive append.

li: please capture cost hit if we disable continuous batching for the model (rough QPS drop and cost delta). we'll need that for PM and infra tradeoff.

sam: rough estimate: with batching disabled effective rps ~25% of baseline and cost per 1k calls +22%. logging that now.

priya: thanks. we'll monitor the adversarial job and decide whether to 1) keep parser fix only, 2) deploy sentinel/index change in eval harness, or 3) ask infra to tweak runtime.

sam: will post job summary + sample failures when 90211 completes. tagging @henry for the infra ticket.

li: ack. good triage.
